You seek to rectify matters at their root and stop troubles at their source. Your examination is meticulous and thorough, and your proposed measures are clear and appropriate. This reveals your learning in statecraft. I have selected this essay in order to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
獻
考試官教諭袁〔廷椿〕批　切實可行有用之士
考試官教諭楊〔舉〕批　有學識有區畫
嘗謂欲實邊者有隨時之權宜有不易之
常道夫足食足兵邊防至要然隨宜以盡
制者一時之權也䘏民而節用者不世之
經也故制有時而可變道無時而可違必
也本吾仁儉之心以施補偏救弊之術夫
然後運量不窮而邊需常裕矣禦戎之策
===
何以加此執事以三邊兵食下詢蓋以識
時務者待承學愚非其人也然亦嘗講求
而有槩于中矣請以所聞爲對今夫天生
五材兵不可無師行糧從食不可去由來
久矣黃虞以前難以殫論粤自成周采薇
之戍杕杜之往蓋不得已焉然而軍寓于
六鄉將取于六卿伍兩卒旅之分茇舍大
閱之講坐聽作止之節掌于大司馬之九
法然又土會土宜土事土均以制斂征徭
punctuated:
獻。
考試官教諭袁〔廷椿〕批：切實可行，有用之士。
考試官教諭楊〔舉〕批：有學識，有區畫。
嘗謂欲實邊者，有隨時之權宜，有不易之常道。夫足食足兵，邊防至要；然隨宜以盡制者，一時之權也；䘏民而節用者，不世之經也。故制有時而可變，道無時而可違。必也本吾仁儉之心，以施補偏救弊之術，夫然後運量不窮，而邊需常裕矣。禦戎之策，何以加此？執事以三邊兵食下詢，蓋以識時務者待承學。愚非其人也，然亦嘗講求，而有槩于中矣。請以所聞爲對。今夫天生五材，兵不可無；師行糧從，食不可去，由來久矣。黃虞以前，難以殫論。粤自成周，《采薇》之戍，《杕杜》之往，蓋不得已焉。然而軍寓于六鄉，將取于六卿；伍兩卒旅之分，茇舍大閱之講，坐聽作止之節，掌于大司馬之九法。然又土會、土宜、土事、土均，以制斂征徭
translation_en:
…for presentation.
Examiner Yuan Tingchun, Instructor, comments: “Practical and feasible: a man fit for service.”
Examiner Yang Ju, Instructor, comments: “He has learning and discernment, and an ability to plan.”
I have often maintained that strengthening the frontier requires both expedients suited to the times and constant principles that do not change. Adequate provisions and troops are essential to frontier defense. Yet adapting institutions to circumstances is an expedient for a particular time; caring for the people and practicing economy is an enduring norm. Thus institutions may sometimes be changed, but the Way may never be transgressed. We must ground ourselves in benevolence and frugality and apply methods that redress imbalances and remedy abuses. Only then will our capacity to manage resources remain inexhaustible and frontier supplies always be ample. What strategy for resisting the Rong could surpass this?
Your Honor has graciously questioned us about troops and provisions in the Three Border Commands, evidently treating us students as men who understand the needs of the times. I, in my ignorance, am not such a man. Nevertheless, I have studied these matters and formed a general conception of them. Allow me to reply on the basis of what I have learned.
Heaven produces the five materials, and weapons cannot be dispensed with; when an army marches, provisions must follow, and food cannot be dispensed with. These truths have long been established. It would be difficult to discuss exhaustively the ages of the Yellow Emperor and Shun and earlier times. From the established Zhou dynasty onward, the garrison service described in “Gathering Bracken” (Cai wei) and the departures described in “The Solitary Pear Tree” (Di du) were surely undertaken only out of necessity. Yet military organization was embedded in the six townships, and commanders were drawn from the six ministers. The division into squads, platoons, companies, and battalions; training in encampment and grand reviews; and the prescribed movements of sitting, listening, rising, and halting were governed by the nine regulations of the Minister of War. Furthermore, assessments of the land, its suitability, its cultivation, and the equalization of its burdens served to regulate collections, taxes, and labor service…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
九賦九貢九式九職以均節財用年不順
成卽有荒政之施一曰散利二曰薄征統
見于司徒太宰之分職是故玁狁于襄虜
公以奏而周爲得策矣降及漢唐非無誼
辟然事窮黷者不曰海內虛耗則爲十道
置兵失富强者不曰上谷被給則爲隴西
失利迄宋則安於承平略於制禦聲容盛
而武備衰議論多而成功少于兵于食舉
無足論矣又何策之有哉洪惟我
===
太祖高皇帝迅掃胡元除兇千古廓清華夏雪
恥百王定鼎
金陵遹崇群構
朝市
陵寢
宮室官署一時荒度費出不貲然且徵兵集
餉尚未息肩而蠲租之
詔無歲不下今年免太平應天之租明年免四
郡三州之賦蘇州屬邑水災免租至四萬
punctuated: 九賦、九貢、九式、九職，以均節財用。年不順成，卽有荒政之施：一曰散利，二曰薄征。統見于司徒、太宰之分職。是故玁狁于襄，虜公以奏，而周爲得策矣。降及漢唐，非無誼辟，然事窮黷者，不曰海內虛耗，則爲十道置兵；失富强者，不曰上谷被給，則爲隴西失利。迄宋，則安於承平，略於制禦，聲容盛而武備衰，議論多而成功少，于兵于食，舉無足論矣，又何策之有哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，迅掃胡元，除兇千古，廓清華夏，雪恥百王。定鼎金陵，遹崇群構，朝市、陵寢、宮室官署，一時荒度，費出不貲。然且徵兵集餉，尚未息肩，而蠲租之詔，無歲不下。今年免太平、應天之租，明年免四郡三州之賦。蘇州屬邑水災，免租至四萬
translation_en:
…the nine levies, nine tribute categories, nine expenditure standards, and nine occupations served to balance and regulate financial resources and expenditure. When the year’s harvest failed, measures for famine relief were put into effect: first, distributing resources; second, reducing taxation. These all appear among the respective duties of the Minister of Education and the Grand Steward. Thus the Xianyun were driven out, and great achievements were accomplished [?; the transcription reads 虜公]. Zhou therefore had an effective strategy.

Coming down to the Han and Tang, there were certainly righteous rulers. Yet those who pursued warfare to the point of exhaustion and recklessness either depleted the resources of the realm or stationed troops throughout the ten circuits. Those who failed to secure wealth and strength either had Shanggu supplied [?] or suffered reverses in Longxi. By the Song, rulers were complacent in settled peace and inattentive to defense. Ceremonial music and display flourished while military preparedness declined; discussions were many, but accomplishments few. In military affairs and provisions alike, there was nothing worth discussing. What strategy could they possibly have had?

We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, who swiftly swept away the non-Han Yuan, eliminated the evil of a thousand ages, cleansed the Chinese realm, and avenged the humiliation of a hundred kings. He established his capital at Jinling and raised its many buildings. The court and markets, imperial mausoleums, palaces, and government offices were all planned and laid out at once, at incalculable expense. Moreover, troops were still being levied and military provisions gathered, with no respite from these burdens. Nevertheless, not a year passed without an edict remitting land taxes. One year he remitted the land taxes of Taiping and Yingtian; the next, the taxes of four prefectures and three subprefectures. When floods struck the counties under Suzhou, the land taxes remitted amounted to forty thousand…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
九千廣德等州旱災免租至七萬六千由
此言之當時之食可知矣況連歲用兵不
暇征戰壘出雖曰
天授
神聖豪傑奮興人皆爲戰兵不求强而自强財
因于敵食不期足而自足要亦我
聖祖躬行節儉勤卹民隱之所致也如浣衣之
服隙地之種
大內宮殿之作惟取堅實亭舘臺榭之禁恐
===
傷民財至
諭中書省臣有曰善治者視民猶己愛而勿
傷不善者徵斂誅求惟日不足又
諭翰林吳沈有曰人君理財之道視國如家
一家之內父子不異貨異貨而家必隳君
民猶父子也損民以益君君獨享富有是
理哉當時食足兵强厥有由也迄我
皇上入繼
大統臨御天下已踰三紀其體
punctuated:
九千，廣德等州旱災，免租至七萬六千。由此言之，當時之食可知矣。況連歲用兵，不暇征戰壘出，雖曰天授神聖，豪傑奮興，人皆爲戰，兵不求强而自强，財因于敵，食不期足而自足，要亦我聖祖躬行節儉、勤卹民隱之所致也。如浣衣之服、隙地之種，大內宮殿之作惟取堅實，亭舘臺榭之禁恐傷民財。至諭中書省臣有曰：「善治者視民猶己，愛而勿傷；不善者徵斂誅求，惟日不足。」又諭翰林吳沈有曰：「人君理財之道，視國如家。一家之內，父子不異貨，異貨而家必隳。君民猶父子也，損民以益君，君獨享富，有是理哉？」當時食足兵强，厥有由也。
迄我皇上入繼大統，臨御天下已踰三紀，其體
translation_en:
…nine thousand. Drought in Guangde and other subprefectures brought tax remissions to seventy-six thousand. From this, the state of grain supplies at the time can be understood. Moreover, troops were deployed year after year, with no respite from warfare and repeated campaigns [?]. Although one might say that Heaven endowed him with sagely wisdom, that heroes rose eagerly, and that everyone fought—so that the army became strong without deliberately seeking strength, and resources were obtained from the enemy, making grain supplies sufficient without expecting sufficiency—these results were also fundamentally due to our sagely founding emperor’s personal practice of frugality and diligent concern for the people’s hardships. Examples include his wearing washed clothing and planting unused ground; in constructing palaces within the imperial residence, he sought only solidity, and he prohibited pavilions, lodges, terraces, and pleasure towers for fear of depleting the people’s resources. He even instructed the officials of the Secretariat: “Those who govern well regard the people as themselves, cherishing them without harming them. Those who govern poorly levy taxes and exact payments, thinking only that each day affords insufficient time.” He also instructed Wu Shen of the Hanlin Academy: “The way for a ruler to manage wealth is to regard the state as his family. Within a family, father and son do not keep separate property; if they do, the family will surely fall apart. Ruler and people are like father and son. Can it be right to impoverish the people to enrich the ruler, leaving the ruler alone to enjoy wealth?” There were indeed reasons why grain was sufficient and the army strong at that time.
Now that our emperor has succeeded to the imperial throne, he has ruled all under Heaven for more than three twelve-year cycles. His embodying…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之心以爲心法
聖祖之治以爲治求䘏民瘼嘉惠元元無所不
至因災而憫有感而興蠲免稅糧凡八下
詔又不啻賑荒施藥散財惠窮而已也夫如是
宜乎財足兵集比隆
皇祖之盛矣夫何邇年以來醜虜不靖邊事頻
殷征調不時轉輸坐困
廟堂之上集議決策隨時立制劑量非不周
詳措置非不曲盡凡以爲兵食之計也顧
===
鹽法設重職矣勢要之請託本折之乾沒
存積利微而商不來私販禁弛而公不售
鹽課其能復昔時之舊乎屯牧添憲臣矣
田在屯亡而隱占典賣者多糧入籍削而
侵欺移貸者半牧地兼幷於勢豪孳息盜
損於圉苑屯牧其能平百姓之情乎冗員
裁矣將士出境而還一人兼三人之給額
外無名孔多一歲預三歲之辦以冗兵動
冗費何侈也逋負督矣頻年拖欠或難責
punctuated: 聖祖之心以爲心，法聖祖之治以爲治，求䘏民瘼，嘉惠元元，無所不至。因災而憫，有感而興，蠲免稅糧，凡八下詔，又不啻賑荒施藥、散財惠窮而已也。夫如是，宜乎財足兵集，比隆皇祖之盛矣。夫何邇年以來，醜虜不靖，邊事頻殷，征調不時，轉輸坐困？廟堂之上，集議決策，隨時立制，劑量非不周詳，措置非不曲盡，凡以爲兵食之計也。顧鹽法設重職矣，勢要之請託，本折之乾沒，存積利微而商不來，私販禁弛而公不售，鹽課其能復昔時之舊乎？屯牧添憲臣矣，田在屯亡，而隱占典賣者多；糧入籍削，而侵欺移貸者半；牧地兼幷於勢豪，孳息盜損於圉苑，屯牧其能平百姓之情乎？冗員裁矣，將士出境而還，一人兼三人之給；額外無名孔多，一歲預三歲之辦。以冗兵動冗費，何侈也！逋負督矣，頻年拖欠，或難責
translation_en:
…the mind of the sagely founder as his own mind, and models his government upon the sagely founder’s government. In seeking to relieve the people’s suffering and bestow blessings upon the common folk, he leaves nothing undone. Moved to compassion by disasters, he acts upon what stirs his concern. He has issued no fewer than eight edicts remitting grain taxes, quite apart from famine relief, the distribution of medicines, and the disbursement of wealth to aid the poor. With measures such as these, surely revenue should be sufficient and troops assembled, matching the flourishing achievements of his imperial ancestor. Why, then, in recent years have the vile northern foes remained unpacified, frontier troubles repeatedly intensified, levies and mobilizations come at irregular intervals, and transport consequently fallen into difficulty? At court, officials deliberate together and decide policy, establishing regulations as circumstances require. Their calculations have certainly been thorough, and their arrangements attentive to every detail—all to provide for troops and their provisions.
Yet although important posts have been established to administer the salt monopoly, there are requests for favors from powerful men and the embezzlement of payments in kind and their cash equivalents. Profits under the reserve-salt system are slight, so merchants do not come; restrictions on illicit trading are lax, so official salt goes unsold. Can salt revenues return to their former level? Additional censorial officials have been appointed to oversee military agricultural colonies and horse pastures. Yet the fields remain while the colonies disappear, and many plots are secretly occupied, mortgaged, or sold. Grain is received while the registers are reduced [?], and embezzlement, fraud, diversion, and lending account for half. Pastureland is engrossed by the powerful, while theft diminishes the breeding stock’s increase in the horse parks. Can the administration of colonies and pastures satisfy the common people?
Superfluous personnel have been reduced. Yet when officers and soldiers return from service beyond the frontier, one man receives the allowances of three. Unauthorized payments beyond the established quotas are exceedingly numerous, and in one year the resources for three years are drawn upon in advance. Superfluous troops generate superfluous expenditure [?]—what extravagance! Collection of arrears has been pressed, yet payments overdue year after year may be difficult to exact…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
于十室九空之家比屋逃亡不易招於百
孔千瘡之日以峻法處窮氓不可也至於
分官催課原非得巳也而望風順旨者曾
石壕吏之不殊召商備儲本以兩便也而
減值增斗者將國門盜之尤劇夫是數者
或代民輸而卒不能繼其始或求
國足而殊不見善其終所謂雖有愛民之心
而民不被其澤者無亦卹民節用之道猶
未盡耳乃切切望于民富而財充食足而
===
兵强不亦難矣哉愚不敢通論天下之勢
姑以生長所目擊者言之夫關中百二之
地四塞之國形勝不必較矣陸海膏壤務
本力穡地不改先秦之闢也帶甲環衛勇
于公戰民不改先秦之聚也當時以一隅
而招八州史固以富强稱之其在於今三
邊列戍八府供傜兵食似非昔日之盛矣
何者
國初邊儲總計不下一百七十餘萬歲不告
punctuated:
于十室九空之家，比屋逃亡，不易招於百孔千瘡之日，以峻法處窮氓，不可也。至於分官催課，原非得巳也，而望風順旨者，曾石壕吏之不殊；召商備儲，本以兩便也，而減值增斗者，將國門盜之尤劇。夫是數者，或代民輸而卒不能繼其始，或求國足而殊不見善其終，所謂雖有愛民之心而民不被其澤者，無亦卹民節用之道猶未盡耳。乃切切望于民富而財充、食足而兵强，不亦難矣哉！
愚不敢通論天下之勢，姑以生長所目擊者言之。夫關中百二之地，四塞之國，形勝不必較矣。陸海膏壤，務本力穡，地不改先秦之闢也；帶甲環衛，勇于公戰，民不改先秦之聚也。當時以一隅而招八州，史固以富强稱之。其在於今，三邊列戍，八府供傜，兵食似非昔日之盛矣。何者？國初邊儲總計不下一百七十餘萬，歲不告
translation_en:
…from households of which nine in ten stand empty. With households everywhere fleeing, it is not easy to summon them back in these days of pervasive devastation. To subject impoverished commoners to harsh laws is unacceptable. As for assigning officials to press for tax payments, this was originally unavoidable; yet those who anticipate their superiors’ wishes and comply with them are no different from the bailiff of Shihao. Inviting merchants to provision the reserves was intended to benefit both sides; yet those who lower the purchase price and enlarge the measuring bushel are even worse than robbers at the capital gates. In these several measures, some advance payments on the people’s behalf but ultimately cannot sustain what they began; others seek to make the state’s resources sufficient, yet their efforts are never seen to end well. These are instances of what is called having a heart that loves the people, while the people receive none of its benefits. Is this not simply because the principles of caring for the people and economizing on expenditure have yet to be fully realized? Yet they earnestly hope that the people will grow wealthy, revenues become abundant, food be sufficient, and the army strong. Is this not difficult indeed?
I, in my ignorance, dare not discuss the circumstances of the whole realm comprehensively. Let me speak only of what I have witnessed in the place where I was born and raised. Guanzhong is a land where two can withstand a hundred, a region protected by barriers on all four sides; its strategic advantages need no comparison. Its fertile soil is a veritable inland sea of abundance, and its people devote themselves to agriculture and labor diligently in the fields: the land remains as extensively cultivated as under Qin before unification. Armored men surround and defend it, courageous in fighting for the state: its people remain as concentrated there as under Qin before unification. In those days, from this single corner Qin drew the eight other regions to itself [?], and the histories indeed praised its wealth and strength. Today, garrisons are arrayed along the Three Frontiers, and the eight prefectures furnish labor service; yet military strength and food supplies seem less flourishing than in former days. Why is this? At the beginning of the dynasty, frontier reserves totaled no less than one million seven hundred thousand and more, and no year brought a report of…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
乏也近則月計不足矣雖增派倍昔旱災
相仍可盡諉之適然之數耶故追償逋負
未免貽牧羊日剪之憂加添歲額正恐坐
抽絲見蛹之患執事慮之誠是也然將何
所措乎夫
京運可乞也不可必也贖金可借也不可盈
也礦場可開也不可訓也傳曰無政事則
財用不足又曰有治人無治法茲欲足食
亦惟有司得其人焉爾巳昔唐遣何庾等
===
爲黜陟使行天下陸贄說以八計聽吏治
內曰計戶口豐耗以稽撫字視墾田羸縮
以稽本末視賦役薄厚以稽廉冒而又以
四賦經財實曰閱稼以奠稅度產以差征
料丁壯以計庸占商賈以均利足食之方
莫備于此今官于秦者誠如贄之言而行
之是其可圖者乎
國初軍數原額二十一萬有奇各邊有定也
今則行伍日空矣雖故絕難勾調遣無常
punctuated:
乏也，近則月計不足矣。雖增派倍昔，旱災相仍，可盡諉之適然之數耶？故追償逋負，未免貽牧羊日剪之憂；加添歲額，正恐坐抽絲見蛹之患。執事慮之，誠是也。然將何所措乎？夫京運可乞也，不可必也；贖金可借也，不可盈也；礦場可開也，不可訓也。傳曰：「無政事則財用不足。」又曰：「有治人，無治法。」茲欲足食，亦惟有司得其人焉爾巳。昔唐遣何庾等爲黜陟使，行天下，陸贄說以八計聽吏治，內曰：「計戶口豐耗以稽撫字，視墾田羸縮以稽本末，視賦役薄厚以稽廉冒。」而又以四賦經財，實曰：「閱稼以奠稅，度產以差征，料丁壯以計庸，占商賈以均利。」足食之方，莫備于此。今官于秦者，誠如贄之言而行之，是其可圖者乎？
國初軍數，原額二十一萬有奇，各邊有定也。今則行伍日空矣。雖故絕難勾，調遣無常，
translation_en:
…there was no shortage. Recently, however, even the monthly reckoning shows a deficit. Although additional levies are twice what they formerly were, and droughts have followed one another, can this all be blamed on the accidents of fate? Pursuing repayment of arrears inevitably raises the concern of a shepherd shearing his sheep every day; increasing the annual quota risks the calamity of reeling away silk until the chrysalis is exposed. Your concern is indeed justified. But what measures should be taken? Shipments from the capital may be requested, but cannot be assured; money from the commutation of punishments may be borrowed, but cannot provide an ample supply; mines may be opened, but this cannot be made a precedent. The transmitted text says: “Without proper administration, financial resources will be insufficient.” It also says: “There are men who bring order, but no laws that bring order of themselves.” To secure sufficient provisions now requires only that the responsible offices be staffed by the right men. Formerly, when the Tang dispatched He Yu [?] and others as commissioners for assessing officials for promotion and demotion throughout the empire, Lu Zhi recommended eight criteria for judging their administration. Among them were: “Calculate the increase or decline in households and population to assess their care for the people; examine the extent and contraction of cultivated land to assess their handling of primary and secondary occupations; examine the lightness or severity of taxes and labor services to assess their integrity or rapacity.” He further proposed managing revenue through four forms of levy, stating: “Inspect the crops to establish taxes; assess property to grade levies; reckon able-bodied adult males to calculate labor-service obligations; register merchants to distribute the profits equitably.” No method of securing sufficient provisions is more comprehensive than this. If those now serving as officials in Qin truly acted according to Lu Zhi’s words, might this not be a practicable course?
At the founding of the dynasty, the original military establishment numbered over 210,000, with fixed allocations for each frontier. Now the ranks grow emptier by the day. Although it is difficult to summon replacements for deceased soldiers and extinguished military households, and troop deployments are irregular…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
可盡付之無可柰何耶然議處民壯以居
守則剜肉醫瘡者何裨遵照糧石以抽丁
則疾首蹙頞者必竄執事憂之非過也策
將何所出乎夫逃亡可解也不可久也班
軍可常也不可用也銀兵可借也不可數
也史曰久守之計須用土兵又曰兵貴精
不貴多茲欲足兵亦惟查抽丁之例調稍
緩之兵暫以役之俟內援既徹而兵漸充
焉爾已昔勝國以蒙古軍居山東河南者
===
戍甘肅當時之臣有言甘肅動涉萬里每
行必鬻田產甚者或賣妻子戍者未歸代
者當發困苦日甚虛殫兵力乞以近甘肅
之兵戍之足兵之計當究于此今領邊計
者誠鑒前說而行之是其可爲者乎雖然
兵食一道用本相須故强國者常患乎財
少富國者不憂其勢弱無已則有鼂錯之
策乎募民徙塞屯營于中使高山遠望部
曲相保塹壘木樵校聯不絕便兵弩飾鬪
punctuated:
可盡付之無可柰何耶？然議處民壯以居守，則剜肉醫瘡者何裨？遵照糧石以抽丁，則疾首蹙頞者必竄。執事憂之，非過也。策將何所出乎？夫逃亡可解也，不可久也；班軍可常也，不可用也；銀兵可借也，不可數也。史曰：「久守之計，須用土兵。」又曰：「兵貴精，不貴多。」茲欲足兵，亦惟查抽丁之例，調稍緩之兵，暫以役之，俟內援既徹而兵漸充焉爾已。昔勝國以蒙古軍居山東、河南者戍甘肅，當時之臣有言：「甘肅動涉萬里，每行必鬻田產，甚者或賣妻子。戍者未歸，代者當發，困苦日甚，虛殫兵力。乞以近甘肅之兵戍之。」足兵之計，當究于此。今領邊計者，誠鑒前說而行之，是其可爲者乎？
雖然，兵食一道，用本相須。故强國者常患乎財少，富國者不憂其勢弱。無已，則有鼂錯之策乎？募民徙塞，屯營于中，使高山遠望，部曲相保，塹壘木樵校聯不絕，便兵弩，飾鬪
translation_en:
…can all this be dismissed as something about which nothing can be done? Yet if able-bodied civilian militiamen are assigned to guard duty, what benefit is there in cutting flesh away to heal a sore? If men are conscripted according to their assessed grain obligations, those driven to anguish and distress will surely flee. Your concern, sir, is not misplaced. What policy, then, can be devised? Deserters can be escorted back [?], but this cannot be sustained indefinitely; troops serving in rotation can be maintained regularly, but cannot be put to effective use; troops hired with silver [?] can be drawn upon, but not repeatedly. The histories say: “For a plan of long-term defense, local troops must be employed.” They also say: “What matters in troops is quality, not numbers.” To secure sufficient troops now, one can only examine the precedents for conscripting men and transfer troops whose duties are somewhat less urgent, employing them temporarily until the reinforcements from the interior have withdrawn and troop strength has gradually been replenished. Formerly, the preceding dynasty sent Mongol troops stationed in Shandong and Henan to garrison Gansu. A minister of that time stated: “Reaching Gansu commonly entails journeys of ten thousand li. Whenever the men set out, they must sell their fields and property; in extreme cases, some even sell their wives and children. Before those on garrison duty have returned, their replacements must depart. Their hardship grows worse by the day, and military strength is exhausted to no purpose. I beg that troops from places near Gansu be used to garrison it.” Plans for securing sufficient troops should investigate this example. If those now directing frontier affairs truly take warning from these earlier arguments and act upon them, might this be something practicable?
Nevertheless, troops and provisions belong to a single undertaking: practical deployment and its material foundation depend upon each other. Thus those who strengthen a state constantly worry about insufficient wealth, while those who enrich a state need not worry that its power is weak. If a further course must be sought, is there not Chao Cuo’s policy? Recruit commoners to move to the frontier and establish fortified settlements there; have them keep watch from high mountains and organize units to protect one another, with trenches, ramparts, and wooden barriers [?] linked without interruption; make ready weapons and crossbows, and put fighting…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
具烽火一通併力合拒以守禦則有人而
外無常戍之勞以屯種則有食而內無轉
輸之費一舉而兩利存充國之所用以却
先零者也是或一道乎要而論之卹民節
用者其本也隨時經制者其權也發乎此
而動乎彼感於上而應於下者其機也故
衡誠設則不可欺以輕重繩誠陳則不可
欺以曲直端本鏡機則綱紀肅而威惠孚
黜貪墨之吏以正風絕夤緣之私以表俗
===
振寬弛之習以作明懲玩愒之漸以袪弊
名實相舛者置以必罰之刑功能未効者
嚴以必禁之令如邊儲也嚴出愼入官吏
不侵其常例而後完納者無停期如軍需
也覈實稽丁將領不列其詭名而後關支
者有實用無窮之浮徵不出而後民以蘇
不時之浪催免行而後人不竄果如是則
邦本可固內地可安縱有不虞之變則子
弟之衞父兄手足之捍頭目將無不至者
punctuated: 具，烽火一通，併力合拒。以守禦則有人，而外無常戍之勞；以屯種則有食，而內無轉輸之費。一舉而兩利存，充國之所用以却先零者也，是或一道乎？要而論之，卹民節用者，其本也；隨時經制者，其權也；發乎此而動乎彼，感於上而應於下者，其機也。故衡誠設，則不可欺以輕重；繩誠陳，則不可欺以曲直。端本鏡機，則綱紀肅而威惠孚。黜貪墨之吏以正風，絕夤緣之私以表俗，振寬弛之習以作明，懲玩愒之漸以袪弊。名實相舛者，置以必罰之刑；功能未効者，嚴以必禁之令。如邊儲也，嚴出愼入，官吏不侵其常例，而後完納者無停期；如軍需也，覈實稽丁，將領不列其詭名，而後關支者有實用。無窮之浮徵不出，而後民以蘇；不時之浪催免行，而後人不竄。果如是，則邦本可固，內地可安。縱有不虞之變，則子弟之衞父兄、手足之捍頭目，將無不至者
translation_en:
…equipment; once the beacon signals are relayed, they can combine their forces to resist together. For defense, there will be men, without the burden of permanent garrison service on the frontier; for farming in military colonies, there will be food, without the expense of transporting supplies from the interior. One measure thus secures two benefits. This was what Chongguo employed to repel the Xianling: might it be one possible course?

To state the essentials: caring for the people and economizing on expenditure are the foundation; devising arrangements suited to the times is the adaptable means; an initiative here producing movement there, and an influence from above eliciting a response below, constitute the pivotal workings. Thus, when a balance is properly set up, one cannot be deceived about weight; when a measuring cord is properly laid out, one cannot be deceived about crookedness and straightness. Set the foundation right and scrutinize these pivotal workings, and discipline will be strict, while authority and benevolence will inspire trust. Dismiss corrupt officials to rectify prevailing conduct; cut off private dealings through connections to set an example for public morals; shake off habits of laxity to promote clear-sighted governance [?]; and check the creeping tendency to idle away time, thereby removing abuses. Those whose actual conduct contradicts their nominal responsibilities must be subjected to penalties that are unfailingly imposed; those whose service has produced no results must be held strictly to prohibitions that are unfailingly enforced.

For frontier stores, strictly control disbursements and carefully oversee receipts. Only when officials and clerks cease taking their customary exactions will those delivering the full amounts due suffer no delays. For military supplies, verify the facts and check the troop rolls. Only when commanders cease listing fictitious names will supplies drawn actually serve their intended purpose. Only when endless additional levies cease to be imposed can the people recover; only when arbitrary demands for payment at irregular times cease can people stop fleeing. If this is indeed done, the foundation of the state can be secured and the interior kept at peace. Even should an unforeseen crisis arise, they will act as sons and younger brothers defending their fathers and elder brothers, or as hands and feet protecting the head and eyes, leaving nothing undone…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
矣又何憂邊防之不靖而狂虜之未恭如
執事之切切者哉草茅之見如此執事儻
與其進尚有程顥廣費之四說蘇軾爲國
之三計以爲
當宁獻
punctuated: 矣。又何憂邊防之不靖，而狂虜之未恭，如執事之切切者哉？草茅之見如此。執事儻與其進，尚有程顥廣費之四說、蘇軾爲國之三計，以爲當宁獻。
translation_en: … indeed. Why, then, should there be such earnest anxiety as yours over unrest along the frontier and the failure of the unruly barbarians to submit? Such are the views of this humble commoner. Should you, sir, approve their presentation, there remain Cheng Hao’s four proposals concerning increased expenditure [?] and Su Shi’s three plans for governing the state, to be offered to His Majesty.

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖壬子秋陝西鄉試錄成
〔廷椿〕以執事寔序末簡諦覽
式文若干篇始焉以喜既而
惕然懼乎爾也乃言曰關洛
之英其在是乎自夫稽訓之
道邈矣拘學抱咫尺之見迂
儒懷淺僿之慚咸無當焉據
===
今所譔表訓勑經典則閑雅
循循不詭于聖謨遡論理源
雜陳時誼弘深奧衍上下數
千百年外史令甲犂然各具
有司馬遷班固之逸軌嗟乎
文之盛也夫摭幹以摛繁則
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖壬子秋，陝西鄉試錄成。〔廷椿〕以執事寔序末簡，諦覽式文若干篇，始焉以喜，既而惕然懼乎爾也。乃言曰：「關洛之英，其在是乎！自夫稽訓之道邈矣，拘學抱咫尺之見，迂儒懷淺僿之慚，咸無當焉。據今所譔，表訓勑經，典則閑雅，循循不詭于聖謨；遡論理源，雜陳時誼，弘深奧衍，上下數千百年，外史令甲，犂然各具有司馬遷、班固之逸軌。嗟乎，文之盛也！夫摭幹以摛繁，則
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the renzi year of Jiajing [1552], the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination was completed. I, 〔Tingchun〕, as one of the officials responsible, wrote a postface on its final leaves. Carefully reading the several model answers, I felt joy at first, but then became apprehensive and fearful. I therefore said: “Are not the outstanding talents of Guan and Luo gathered here? The way of examining the teachings of antiquity has long grown remote. Narrow scholars cling to circumscribed views, while pedantic scholars harbor shame at their own shallowness: neither measures up.

“Judging by the compositions now before us, they set forth instruction and put the classics in order [?], displaying classical propriety and cultivated elegance, methodically following the sages’ counsels without departing from them. They trace their arguments to the sources of principle and present a variety of considerations appropriate to the times. Broad and profound, subtle and expansive, they range over hundreds and thousands of years. Unofficial histories and statutory ordinances are clearly distinguished, each composition displaying the extraordinary literary achievement of Sima Qian and Ban Gu. Ah, what flourishing literary accomplishment! When one takes hold of the trunk to unfold its luxuriant branches, then …”

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
敷揚者碩濬淵以析支則沿
流者長三輔歷代故都類多
豪宕出群之士而
國朝培養篤至鴻宗碩學踵繼
肩連第其稟賦沉厚朴外深
中無幾微現諸顏色而含毫
授簡摛藻吐詞往往發舒崛
===
奇縱橫之思雲翔霧擁見者
駭神海內以文章名家者率
不能下玆其華實並著云古
人有言曰文貌繁情欲省禮
之隆也文貌省情欲繁禮之
殺也文貌情欲並行而雜禮
之中流也質植文宣言焉益
punctuated: 敷揚者碩，濬淵以析支，則沿流者長。三輔歷代故都，類多豪宕出群之士，而國朝培養篤至，鴻宗碩學踵繼肩連。第其稟賦沉厚，朴外深中，無幾微現諸顏色；而含毫授簡，摛藻吐詞，往往發舒崛奇縱橫之思，雲翔霧擁，見者駭神。海內以文章名家者，率不能下玆，其華實並著云。古人有言曰：「文貌繁，情欲省，禮之隆也；文貌省，情欲繁，禮之殺也；文貌情欲並行而雜，禮之中流也。」質植文宣，言焉益
translation_en:
…what is expounded is grand; when the depths are plumbed to distinguish the branches, the streams flowing from them run far. The Sanfu region, the site of successive dynastic capitals, has commonly produced bold, unrestrained men of outstanding talent. Our dynasty has nurtured them with the utmost care: eminent masters and great scholars have followed one another, shoulder to shoulder. Yet their natural disposition is composed and substantial, plain outwardly and profound within, with not the slightest stirring showing in their faces. When they take up brush and writing tablet, however, and unfold their elegant language, they often give expression to strikingly original and freely ranging thoughts, like soaring clouds and gathering mist, astonishing all who see them. Those renowned throughout the realm as masters of literary composition generally cannot rank these men beneath themselves [?]. Their outward brilliance and inner substance are thus both manifest.
An ancient said: “When patterned forms and outward observances abound, while feelings and desires are restrained, ritual is at its height. When patterned forms and outward observances are few, while feelings and desires abound, ritual is in decline. When patterned forms, outward observances, feelings, and desires proceed together and intermingle, ritual occupies the middle course.” With substance firmly rooted and literary refinement made manifest, their words become ever more…

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遠其先民之遺則中流之準
乎或謂浮習罔諧焉謬也故
其希聲茂采金石鏗鉤可以
廉頑可以肅眾而武以揚矣
從容暇整統統而思斷斷而
辯也而文以明矣贍洽而浩
博廣賁而清通出之無窮用
===
===
之不究可以經國之治而不
泥焉雕蟲之技文質之中士
之紀也四方將訏謨是度以
遵厥成其疇能易之雖然文
以飾治質以敦本飾治則物
用昭敦本則思言永將不虞
文之靡稱而鮮克有終行也
alt_text:
遠其先民之遺則中流之準
乎或謂浮習罔諧焉謬也故
其希聲茂采金石鏗鍧可以
廉頑可以肅衆而武以揚矣
從容暇整�William
===
遠其先民之遺則中流之準
乎或謂浮習罔諧焉謬也故
其希聲茂采金石鏗鍧可以
廉頑可以肅衆而武以揚矣
從容暇整紞紞而思斷斷而
辯也而文以明矣贍洽而浩
博廣賾而清通出之無窮用
之不究可以經國之治而不
===
泥焉雕蟲之技文質之中士
之紀也四方將訏謨是度以
遵厥成其疇能易之雖然文
以飾治質以敦本飾治則物
用昭敦本則思言求將不虞
文之靡稱而鮮克有終行也
punctuated: 遠。其先民之遺則、中流之準乎？或謂浮習罔諧焉，謬也。故其希聲茂采，金石鏗鉤，可以廉頑，可以肅眾，而武以揚矣。從容暇整，統統而思，斷斷而辯也，而文以明矣。贍洽而浩博，廣賁而清通，出之無窮，用之不究，可以經國之治，而不泥焉雕蟲之技。文質之中，士之紀也。四方將訏謨是度，以遵厥成，其疇能易之？雖然，文以飾治，質以敦本。飾治則物用昭，敦本則思言永。將不虞文之靡稱，而鮮克有終。行也，
translation_en: …farther. Is this the pattern bequeathed by the ancients, the standard of the middle course? Some say that superficial habits cannot accord with it; this is mistaken. Thus its rarefied sounds and splendid ornament resound like bronze and stone instruments [?]; they can make the obstinate upright and instill reverence in the multitude, thereby displaying martial vigor. Composed, unhurried, and orderly, comprehensive in thought [?] and earnest in argument, it thereby makes civil refinement manifest. Ample and all-embracing, vast and extensive, richly adorned yet lucid and coherent, it issues forth inexhaustibly and cannot be exhausted in use. It can serve the governance of the realm without becoming mired in the petty craft of carving insects—that is, merely ornamental writing. The proper balance of literary refinement and substance is the guiding standard for scholars. Throughout the realm, men will consider grand plans and follow established accomplishments: who could alter this standard? Nevertheless, literary refinement embellishes governance, while substance strengthens the foundation. When governance is embellished, affairs become manifest; when the foundation is strengthened, thought and speech endure. There may be no fear that literary refinement will fail to measure up, yet few can carry it through to the end. As for conduct, …

title: 嘉靖三十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
嚴矣諸士玆彬彬爾而嚴之
行焉能無貽主司之懼也歟
哉是用勗之
四川成都府溫江縣儒學教
諭袁〔廷椿〕謹序
punctuated:
嚴矣！諸士玆彬彬爾，而嚴之行焉，能無貽主司之懼也歟哉？是用勗之。
四川成都府溫江縣儒學教諭袁〔廷椿〕謹序。
translation_en:
…is exacting indeed! You gentlemen now display a harmonious balance of refinement and substance; yet, when exacting standards are applied to your conduct [?], can you avoid giving those presiding over the examination cause for apprehension? This is why I offer you this exhortation.
Preface respectfully composed by Yuan Tingchun, Instructor in the Confucian School of Wenjiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan.
